title: Simple Resignation Letter Template
description: Free professional resignation letter template you can copy, edit, and use for leaving a job professionally.
intro: This simple resignation letter template helps employees formally resign from a position while keeping communication professional and respectful.
whenToUse: Use this template when leaving a job and providing formal written notice.

Dear [Manager Name],

I am writing to formally resign from my position at [Company Name], effective [Last Working Day].

Thank you for the opportunities and support during my time with the company.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]

intro: This recommendation letter template helps managers and supervisors provide positive, professional references for employees.
whenToUse: Use this template when writing references for employees applying to new jobs, promotions, or professional programs.
template:
To Whom It May Concern,

I am pleased to recommend [Employee Name] for [Position or Opportunity]. [Employee Name] has been employed at [Company Name] as a [Job Title] since [Start Date] and consistently demonstrated [Key Strengths].

Their strengths include [Strength 1], [Strength 2], and [Strength 3]. I believe they would be a strong asset to your team.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
[Title]
example:
To Whom It May Concern,

I am pleased to recommend Michael Park for the Senior Operations Manager role. Michael has been employed at Summit Logistics as Operations Coordinator since 2021 and consistently demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and strong communication.

His strengths include process improvement, team collaboration, and attention to detail. I believe he would be a strong asset to your team.

Sincerely,
Karen Lee
Operations Director
tips: Highlight the employee’s strongest skills and achievements.
Keep the tone positive, honest, and concise.
Include specific examples when possible.
Sign and date the letter for credibility.

faqs.question: Who should write employee recommendation letters?
faqs.answer: Managers, supervisors, or mentors who know the employee’s work are the best writers.

faqs.question: What should be included in a recommendation letter?
faqs.answer: Include the employee’s role, strengths, accomplishments, and suitability for the opportunity.

faqs.question: Can recommendation letters be requested after leaving a job?
faqs.answer: Yes, former employers can still provide references if they agree.

title: Employment Verification Letter for Loan Applications
description: Employment verification letter template for loan and financing applications.
intro: This employment verification letter template helps borrowers provide proof of employment and income for loan applications.
whenToUse: Use this letter when a lender or financial institution requires employment verification for mortgage, personal, or business loans.
template:
To Whom It May Concern,

This letter confirms that [Employee Name] is employed with [Company Name] as a [Job Title]. [Employee Name] has been employed since [Start Date].

Current employment status: [Full-Time/Part-Time]
Annual salary: [Salary]

If additional information is needed, please contact us at [Phone Number] or [Email Address].

Sincerely,
[Employer Name]
[Company Name]
example:
To Whom It May Concern,

This letter confirms that Maria Chen is employed with BlueTree Finance as a Senior Analyst. Maria has been employed since August 2021.

Current employment status: Full-Time
Annual salary: $82,000

If additional information is needed, please contact us at 555-123-4567 or hr@bluetreefinance.com.

Sincerely,
Rachel Ortiz
BlueTree Finance
tips: Include accurate employment dates and salary details.
Use official letterhead when available.
Confirm the employee’s job title before sending.
Provide employer contact information for verification.

faqs.question: What is an employment verification letter for loans?
faqs.answer: It is a document confirming employment details and income for a lender’s review.

faqs.question: Should salary be included?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the lender requests income verification.

faqs.question: Who signs this letter?
faqs.answer: A manager, HR representative, or authorized employer contact typically signs it.

title: Termination Letter Template for Contractors
description: Contractor termination letter template for ending service agreements.
intro: This contractor termination letter template helps businesses formally end contractor engagements while documenting the reason and next steps.
whenToUse: Use this template when ending a contractor or consultant agreement due to completion, performance issues, or changing business needs.
template:
Dear [Contractor Name],

This letter serves as formal notice that your contract with [Company Name] will end effective [Termination Date].

Reason: [Reason] 

Please return any company materials and submit all final deliverables by your termination date.

Thank you for your work and cooperation.

Sincerely,
[Manager Name]
[Company Name]
example:
Dear Jordan Lee,

This letter serves as formal notice that your contract with Greenfield Media will end effective June 30, 2026.

Reason: Project scope has been completed.

Please submit final deliverables and return any company assets by your termination date.

Thank you for your work.

Sincerely,
Avery Brooks
Greenfield Media
tips: State the termination date and reason clearly.
Clarify expectations for final deliverables and asset returns.
Keep the tone professional and respectful.
Confirm whether any outstanding payments remain.

faqs.question: What is a contractor termination letter?
faqs.answer: It is a formal notice that a contractor’s engagement is ending.

faqs.question: Should contractors be given notice?
faqs.answer: Yes, provide notice consistent with the contract terms.

faqs.question: Do contractor terminations need a reason?
faqs.answer: A brief reason is useful for documentation and clarity.

[Employer Name]
[Employee Name]

title: Cover Letter Template for Teaching Positions
description: Teaching job cover letter template for educators.
intro: This cover letter template helps teachers highlight classroom experience, instructional strengths, and dedication to student success.
whenToUse: Use this template when applying for teaching jobs, educational roles, or school leadership positions.
template:
Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to apply for the [Teaching Position] at [School Name]. With experience teaching [Grade Level/Subject], I have developed strong classroom management and lesson planning skills.

In my current role at [School], I implemented [Program or Achievement] that improved student engagement.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
example:
Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to apply for the 5th Grade Teacher position at Oak Valley Elementary School. With experience teaching English Language Arts and social studies, I have built engaging lessons that support literacy and critical thinking.

In my current role at Maple Ridge Elementary, I implemented a reading program that increased student participation by 20%.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Cassie Rivera
tips: Mention teaching experience and subject expertise.
Highlight positive student outcomes and classroom achievements.
Tailor the letter to the school’s mission and culture.
Keep the letter concise and professional.

faqs.question: Should teaching cover letters mention student success?
faqs.answer: Yes, highlighting student outcomes strengthens your application.

faqs.question: Can a teacher use a generic cover letter?
faqs.answer: It’s better to customize the letter for each school or role.

faqs.question: What should a teacher include in a cover letter?
faqs.answer: Include experience, instructional strengths, and reasons you’re a good fit.

title: Termination Letter Template for Employers

template:
Dear [Employee Name],

This letter confirms that your employment with [Company Name] will end effective [Termination Date].

[Manager Name]
[Company Name]

Cedar Point Digital

faqs.question: Should I keep a copy of the termination letter?

faqs.question: Can a termination letter be contested?

Lender: [Name]
Amount: [Amount]
Repayment Terms: [Schedule]
Date: [Date]

Borrower Signature: __________
example:
Promissory Note

Borrower: Tim Green
Lender: Sara Park
Amount: $1,000
Repayment Terms: $100/month for 10 months
Date: April 5, 2026

faqs.question: Should it be notarized?
faqs.answer: Not required in many cases but notarization can add formality and provenance.

title: Simple Affidavit
description: A basic affidavit template for sworn statements.
intro: Use this affidavit template to provide a sworn written statement of facts.
whenToUse: When a sworn statement is needed for legal or administrative purposes.
template:
Affidavit

I, [Name], state under oath that: [Statement].

Signed: __________
Date: [Date]
example:
Affidavit

I, Alex Rivera, state under oath that I witnessed the property damage on March 10, 2026.

Signed: Alex Rivera

faqs.question: Do affidavits need notarization?
faqs.answer: Often yes; check local rules for sworn statements.

title: Flat-Rate Service Invoice
description: Invoice template for flat-rate services.

whenToUse: Billing clients for project-based, flat-fee services.
template:
Invoice #: [Number]
Date: [Date]
Service: [Description]
Amount: [Total]
Due: [Date]

Invoice #: 3001
Date: May 10, 2026
Service: Website redesign
Amount: $3,000
Due: June 10, 2026

faqs.question: What payment terms to include?
faqs.answer: Include due date and accepted payment methods.

title: Basic Project Proposal
description: A simple proposal template to outline scope and pricing.

whenToUse: When pitching services or projects to clients.
template:
Proposal Title: [Project]
Client: [Name]
Scope: [Deliverables]
Timeline: [Dates]
Cost: [Amount]

Proposal Title: Branding Refresh
Client: Greenleaf Co.
Scope: Logo, color palette, basic guidelines
Timeline: 4 weeks
Cost: $4,500

faqs.question: Should I include payment milestones?
faqs.answer: Yes — they help manage expectations and cash flow.

title: Meeting Agenda Template
description: A simple meeting agenda to keep discussions focused.

whenToUse: Before scheduled meetings to share topics and time allocations.
template:
Meeting: [Topic]
Date: [Date]
Attendees: [Names]
Agenda:
- [Item 1]
- [Item 2]

Meeting: Project Kickoff
Date: May 18, 2026
Attendees: PM, Designer, Dev
Agenda:
- Scope review
- Timeline
- Next steps

faqs.question: How long should agendas be?
faqs.answer: Keep items focused and assign time estimates for each.

title: Simple Consulting Agreement
description: A concise consulting agreement for short-term engagements.

Fee: [Amount]

Term: May 2026

faqs.question: Should consultants have NDAs?
faqs.answer: Often yes — include confidentiality provisions if needed.

title: Formal Apology Letter
description: A template to apologize professionally and restore relationships.
intro: Use this letter to offer a sincere, professional apology.
whenToUse: When you need to apologize formally to colleagues, friends, or partners.
template:
Dear [Name],

I want to apologize for [Action]. I understand the impact and will [Remedy].

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
example:
Dear Alex,

I’m sorry for missing our meeting and not giving advance notice. I’ll ensure better communication going forward.

Sincerely,
Riley

faqs.question: How sincere should the apology be?
faqs.answer: Be honest, accept responsibility, and outline steps to make amends.

title: Short Thank-You Note
description: A brief thank-you note for interviews or favors.
intro: A concise, polite thank-you message you can send quickly.
whenToUse: After interviews, informational meetings, or receiving help.
template:
Hi [Name],

Thank you for [Help/Time]. I appreciate it and look forward to staying in touch.

Best,
[Your Name]
example:
Hi Dana,

Thanks for taking the time to review my portfolio — I appreciate your feedback.

Best,
Sam

faqs.question: When to send?
faqs.answer: Within 24–48 hours is best.

title: Simple Reference Letter

I am pleased to recommend [Name] for [Opportunity]. [They] have demonstrated [Strengths].

Sincerely,
[Your Name]

To Whom It May Concern,

I recommend Priya Patel for volunteer coordinator role. Priya is organized, dependable, and a strong communicator.

Sincerely,
L. Gomez

faqs.question: What to include?
faqs.answer: Specific examples and your relationship to the person.

I am resigning to pursue an opportunity that will support my career growth. My last day will be [Date].

Sincerely,
[Name]

I am resigning to accept a role that aligns with my long-term goals. My last day will be July 10, 2026.

Sincerely,
Ethan

Sincerely,
[Name]

Sincerely,
Nora

[Name]

Thanks,
Taylor
